title: Fomo Kernel Trade Premise
description: One hypothetical trade the model or user supplies mid-decision ('I'm thinking of buying NVDA — what does that do to my book?'). This is Layer 2 (docs/decision-fomo-kernel-shape.md §3): deterministic arithmetic over a premise, never a recommendation. The readable contract; skills/fomo-kernel/engine/consequence.py's validate_premise holds the enforcement, because the offline suite carries no jsonschema dependency. The envelope's field rules are stated once, here — consequence.py does not restate them, only enforces them.

ticker.description: The complete engine symbol, in the same form the ledger's own rows use (for example NVDA, 2330.TW). Matching the ledger's convention is what lets before/after states compare the same instrument rather than two strings that merely look alike.

side.description: Which direction the hypothetical trade goes. A sell is checked against what is currently held (a sell of an unheld ticker, or more shares than are held, is refused rather than silently clamped or read as a short) because this layer computes consequences of a real position change, not a speculative short thesis.

price.description: The hypothetical execution price, in the instrument's own trading currency. Required even when notional is given, because notional is converted to a share count by dividing through this price — the engine's downstream arithmetic is share-based, matching how the ledger itself is recorded.

qty.description: Hypothetical share count. Mutually exclusive with notional (oneOf below) — the caller states the trade the one way they actually have it in mind, and the engine derives the other, rather than both being supplied and silently disagreeing.

notional.description: Hypothetical trade size in cash terms (this instrument's currency). Converted to qty via notional / price. Mutually exclusive with qty.

date.description: When the hypothetical trade would happen. Optional — defaults to the day after the ledger's last row, so an unstated premise reads as 'if I did this next' rather than silently backdating into history. A date earlier than the last ledger row is refused: this layer computes a forward consequence, not a rewrite of what already happened.

currency.description: Trading currency of the price. Optional — defaults to the ticker's own currency in the ledger when it is already held, or USD for a new position, so an omitted currency cannot silently mis-aggregate a mixed-currency book.
